item.title: [ 39] All major US broadcasters boycott Trump over press ban
item.description:
https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2026/09/21/politico-and-cnn-sue-trump-over-white-house-ban/

All major US TV networks are boycotting Donald Trump’s official engagements after he banned CNN from the White House.

Mr Trump said on Friday he was banning the network – along with MS NOW and Politico – shortly after he was reportedly shown clips by his aide Natalie Harp of MS NOW anchors criticising his administration on air.

The announcement apparently came as a surprise to many of Mr Trump’s advisers.

But he is known to be particularly fond of Ms Harp, who has earned the nickname of “the human printer” because she is responsible for handing him printouts of news reports or other important information.

CNN had been scheduled on Monday to be the “TV pool” camera crew, which is responsible for following the president and broadcasting his engagements to all networks.

The pooled coverage duty rotates among the major news networks, which then share the footage with each other.

CNN was removed from its pooled coverage responsibilities following Mr Trump’s ban.

But the other news networks in the pool – Fox News, NBC, ABC and CBS – decided not to provide a replacement in solidarity with CNN, marking a major escalation in the feud between Mr Trump and the media.

“The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organisation because it objects to its reporting,” a joint statement from the five networks said.

An email sent to TV pool subscribers on Monday said: “Effective today, the TV pool will not be covering events designated as pool coverage of the president,” according to CNN.

item.title: [111] Just in time for midterms, Trump's approval dips below 30 percent
item.description:
https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-approval-rating-hits-all-time-low-12467727

President Donald Trump's approval rating dropped below 30 percent for the first time across both his White House terms Monday, as the midterms draw closer.

The new poll, from American Research Group, conducted September 16-20 among 1,100 American adults, showed the president with a 29 percent overall approval rating, with positive views on the economy at 26 percent.

Overall, 72 percent of those surveyed said they felt the U.S. economy was getting worse amid rising gas and grocery prices despite the Trump administration's insistence that those pressures are still largely down to the previous administration.

By comparison, other recent polls have generally shown Trump with approval in the mid-to-high 30s, although that has differed depending on policy areas.

The last time a president's approval was in the 20s was President George W. Bush at the end of 2008, per Gallup's presidential approval tracker.

"This poll is an outlier, as others are not as bleak for the president, but overall it's pretty clear that Trump's numbers are worse now than they were eight years ago," Kyle Kondik, from the University of Virginia's Center for Politics, told Newsweek. "Dissatisfaction with the economy/inflation is probably the biggest reason why."

Newsweek reached out to the White House for comment Monday morning.

https://nypost.com/2026/09/20/us-news/nyt-writer-nikole-hannah-jones-sent-daughter-to-troubled-schools-as-a-sacrifice-and-it-backfired/
The writer behind the New York Times’ controversial 1619 Project deliberately sent her daughter to poor Big Apple schools as a “sacrifice” to try to boost the education system — and no one is angrier than the kid.

The teen is now “boiling” mad — badly behind her peers after finally being allowed to enroll in a more rigorous high school, her mother revealed in a bombshell bizarre essay.

Nikole Hannah-Jones, 50, enrolled her only child in two struggling Brooklyn public schools beginning in 2015 — as part of a battle to change what she characterized as systemic racism, despite having the “connections and time and status” to get the girl into the city’s best schools, she wrote in the Times Magazine on Sunday.
“So you had money to send me to one of the best schools, and you chose not to?” the girl yelled in one fight, according to the essay. “Because other kids are disadvantaged, you didn’t want to put me in a great school?”

Hannah-Jones wrote of her decision, “We thought by sending Najya to a mostly low-income and Black school, we could help improve it for all the children there.

“We believed strongly that if families like ours went into schools like this one, it would challenge other families with similar values to do the same.

“I felt an obligation to make educational decisions based on the collective good and not just our individual advantage,” the mom said.

But after years of her daughter at the schools — PS 307 and Urban Assembly Unison, a specialty middle school — Hannah-Jones discovered her sharp-witted child lacked the basic skills to keep up in high school.


“Sometimes I wish instead of always thinking about other kids, you would have thought about me,” Hannah-Jones’ now-16-year-old daughter, Najya, said during a confrontation over the summer.

“I never really got the education I wanted.”

item.title: [ 34] Russia Holds Elections in Annexed Regions of Ukraine
item.description:
Thread theme: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Qmezd5yTGRQ

https://www.npr.org/2026/09/19/g-s1-144169/russia-holds-parliamentary-vote-in-areas-it-seized-from-ukraine

Russia's parliamentary election for the first time includes residents of regions that Moscow illegally annexed from Ukraine after the start of its full-scale invasion more than 4 1/2 years ago, part of Kremlin efforts to cement its gains.

Officials in Kyiv vigorously denounced the action as illegal, and a human rights activist described residents there as being coerced to participate in the election.

While the vote across Russia started Friday and lasts until Sunday to help boost turnout, balloting actually has been underway in the annexed parts of Ukraine and some areas on the Russian side of the border since the end of last month. Officials cited security reasons for the extended period.

Russian authorities say the Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia territories, often referred to by Moscow officials as the "new regions," have over 3.5 million voters. They were annexed by Russia in September 2022, despite not fully being under Moscow's control. The move has not been recognized internationally.

At one polling station in the Russian-held part of the Donetsk region, voters dropped their ballots in a box as an armed Russian soldier stood nearby and watched.

In a speech Wednesday, Russian President Vladimir Putin emphasized the importance of balloting in those regions for the State Duma, the lower house of parliament. Residents there will be voting for the Duma "for the first time since their reunification with Russia."

He noted that Russian soldiers involved in the fighting also will vote.

Voting also is taking place in Crimea, the Black Sea peninsula that was illegally annexed by Moscow in 2014.

The first wartime election to the State Duma is intended to secure the Kremlin's political dominance and showcase public support for the war.

item.title: [ 42] How dangerous is solo backpacking? I live close to Appalachia and any time I ta
item.description:
How dangerous is solo backpacking? I live close to Appalachia and any time I talk to someone about going on a solo trip people talk schitzo-tier about how I'm going to die, disappear, or worse.
Not even because of the nature specifically, but because of le paranormal, inbred mountain people, cannibals, accidentally stumbling upon illegal operations in the mountains (heard this one specifically a lot), etc. You get it, the list goes on.
Anyways, is there any truth to the danger or is it just the average small-town tall tales and superstitions? Seems unlikely to me as I feel like if it was so dangerous you'd be seeing a lot more of it in the news.
